# Source and Claim Verification

1. Prefer primary official documentation, regulator sources, source repositories, and direct tests.
2. Record URL, title, publisher, verification date, applicable version/region, and exact claim.
3. Mark claims verified, unverified, contradicted, or needs investigation.
4. Check existence, internal consistency, counter-hypotheses, commercial restrictions, limits, deprecations, and source freshness.
5. Never turn a relevance score, vendor marketing statement, or mechanism spike into a trust/safety/production claim.
6. Public claims require owner, evidence, scope/baseline, approval, review cadence, expiry, and correction/removal action.
